reference_corpus: Weekly reminder loops improve meal adherence by keeping the plan visible.
Simple grocery automation can reduce weekday cooking friction for busy users.
Nutrition motivation loops often fail when the user runs out of time on weekdays.

candidates.claim: Pre-committed Sunday ingredient batching may reduce weekday meal skipping for time-scarce users.
candidates.mechanism: Batching lowers weekday prep friction and preserves a visible cue, so the user reaches for the prepared option before time pressure breaks adherence.
candidates.evidence_needed: Compare weekday skip rate, prep time, and completion rate between a batching cohort and a no-batching cohort across four weeks.
candidates.falsifier: If skip rate does not improve after batching even when prep time falls, the friction mechanism is wrong.
known_risks: Selection bias toward users who already like planning.
Weekend batching may itself become a burden for some users.
candidates.wellness_boundary: Wellness coaching only. Not diagnosis or treatment.
alternative_explanations: The batching group may already have stronger planning habits.
Calendar reminders may explain the adherence gain more than batching.
counterevidence: Users with full prep access may still skip meals under stress.
candidates.stopping_rule: Stop after four weeks if skip rate and prep time both fail to improve.
candidates.decision_rule: Promote only if skip rate improves without a matching rise in prep burden.
candidates.minimum_observation: At least four weeks across two comparable cohorts.

candidates.claim: Run a crossover experiment that alternates lunch templates versus open-ended meal choice during workdays.
candidates.mechanism: Fixed templates reduce choice overload, which should free attention for execution rather than daily planning.
candidates.evidence_needed: Measure adherence, decision time, and perceived friction in an A/B crossover design over two two-week periods.
candidates.falsifier: If adherence stays flat during template weeks despite lower decision time, the choice-overload explanation fails.
known_risks: Novelty effects may decay after the first week.
candidates.wellness_boundary: Wellness coaching only. Not diagnosis or treatment.
alternative_explanations: Lunch adherence may rise because the template week also simplifies shopping.
counterevidence: Adherence may improve even when decision time does not change.
candidates.stopping_rule: Stop after the second crossover period if decision time and adherence both stay flat.
candidates.decision_rule: Promote only if template weeks reduce decision time and improve adherence together.
candidates.minimum_observation: Two two-week periods in the crossover sequence.

candidates.claim: Unexpected weekend adherence drops may come from grocery depletion rather than motivation loss.
candidates.mechanism: The pantry is progressively depleted by Friday, so weekend adherence drops because the easiest planned foods are no longer available.
candidates.evidence_needed: Track pantry completeness, grocery restock timing, and weekend adherence across several weeks to test the depletion signal.
candidates.falsifier: If weekend drops persist when pantry completeness stays high, grocery depletion is not the main explanation.
known_risks: Self-reported pantry data may be noisy.
candidates.wellness_boundary: Wellness coaching only. Not diagnosis or treatment.
alternative_explanations: Weekend schedule changes may matter more than pantry depletion.
counterevidence: Weekend adherence may recover even when pantry completeness is low.
candidates.stopping_rule: Stop after several weekends if pantry completeness does not track the adherence drop.
candidates.decision_rule: Promote only if pantry completeness predicts the weekend drop better than motivation cues.
candidates.minimum_observation: Several consecutive weeks including at least three weekends.
